title.value: ISO 26262-1:2018 Road vehicles — Functional safety — Part 1: Vocabulary

scope.value: Publisher catalog metadata scopes Part 1 to vocabulary for a functional-safety framework addressing hazards caused by malfunctioning behaviour of safety-related road-vehicle E/E systems and identifies exclusions.

comparator.value: ISO 21448:2022 catalog scope for intended-function insufficiency, plus proposed Reiyah protocol reiyah.protocol.harbor-gate-a@1.1.0 as an architecture-only target with no conformance baseline.

requirement_locator.value: ISO Open Data record 68383 fields reference, publicationDate, edition, currentStage, replacedBy, and scope; no normative clause locator is retained.

entries.proposed_relevance: The metadata suggests a useful architecture boundary between evidence about malfunctioning behaviour and evidence about intended-function or model insufficiency. Reiyah proposes to preserve that distinction; it does not implement an ISO 26262 lifecycle or claim alignment.

gap.description: Only a publisher catalog record for Part 1 is retained, while the ISO 26262 series text, relevant clauses, interpretations, later parts, and in-development successor are absent.
closure_requirements: Lawfully obtain and retain the exact normative editions and parts selected for a future mapping, including licence and access constraints.
Have a qualified independent reviewer identify exact clauses, applicability, exclusions, and the relationship to the then-current ISO revision.
Define a separately authorized protocol-level comparator before evaluating any alignment or conformance question.

title.value: ISO 21448:2022 Road vehicles — Safety of the intended functionality

scope.value: Publisher catalog metadata describes an argument framework and guidance for hazards from intended-function specification or performance insufficiencies, including situational awareness derived from complex sensors and processing, foreseeable misuse, and declared exclusions.

comparator.value: ISO 26262-1:2018 publisher scope for malfunctioning E/E behaviour, plus proposed Reiyah protocol reiyah.protocol.harbor-gate-a@1.1.0 with no implementation or conformance target.

requirement_locator.value: ISO Open Data record 77490 fields reference, publicationDate, edition, currentStage, replacedBy, and scope; no normative clause locator is retained.

entries.proposed_relevance: The retained scope summary suggests that unknown scenarios, functional insufficiencies, situational-awareness limits, and foreseeable misuse are relevant boundary categories for an evidence engine. Reiyah proposes only to keep those categories distinguishable from faults and outcomes.

gap.description: The full 181-page standard, its clauses, evidence expectations, and pending successor are not retained, so no requirements-level mapping is possible.
closure_requirements: Lawfully obtain and retain the exact ISO 21448 edition selected for review and its applicable successor status.
Commission an independent clause-level review that distinguishes SOTIF terminology from Reiyah's proposed constructs and validity states.
Define falsifiable protocol comparisons without converting a scope similarity into a safety or compliance claim.

title.value: ISO/PAS 8800:2024 Road vehicles — Safety and artificial intelligence

scope.value: Publisher catalog metadata scopes the PAS to safety-related road-vehicle systems using AI and describes output insufficiencies, systematic errors, random hardware errors, external AI interactions, and safety-related properties for assurance arguments.

comparator.value: ISO 21448:2022 publisher scope for intended-function insufficiency, compared only at metadata level with proposed Reiyah protocol reiyah.protocol.harbor-gate-a@1.1.0.

requirement_locator.value: ISO Open Data record 83303 fields reference, publicationDate, edition, currentStage, replacedBy, and scope; no PAS clause locator is retained.

entries.proposed_relevance: The metadata suggests future evidence categories for AI output insufficiency, systematic error, hardware error, and external-element interaction. Gate A proposes provenance and explicit-invalidity structures that may later be compared with those categories; it authorizes no AI runtime or safety assurance claim.

gap.description: The 172-page PAS and its safety-related properties are not retained, and the catalog record lists two unretained replacement projects.
closure_requirements: Lawfully retain the exact PAS text and metadata for any successor selected at the time of future review.
Obtain independent automotive AI-safety review of exact clauses, scope exclusions, assurance semantics, and successor relationships.
Keep any future mapping separate from an assurance, certification, safety, or compliance conclusion.

title.value: ISO/TR 21959-1:2020 Road vehicles — Human performance and state in the context of automated driving — Part 1: Common underlying concepts

scope.value: Publisher catalog metadata describes informative common concepts for driver performance and state where a driver is engaged, fallback-ready, or able to resume manual control, including simulator, restricted-road, and public-road evaluations.

comparator.value: The proposed Reiyah readiness estimand in reiyah.protocol.harbor-gate-a@1.1.0; the external report's concepts and Reiyah's protocol-bound readiness construct are not treated as equivalent.

requirement_locator.value: ISO Open Data record 78088 fields reference, publicationDate, edition, currentStage, and scope; the retained metadata explicitly says the report is informative, and no report clause is retained.

entries.proposed_relevance: The scope is directly adjacent to human-automation readiness terminology and experimental contexts. It is retained to prevent Reiyah from inventing a confident one-score synonym for driver state, not as evidence that Reiyah's readiness definition is valid or standardized.

gap.description: Only metadata and the informative scope summary are available; the report's definitions, research gaps, evaluation considerations, and cited evidence are absent.
closure_requirements: Lawfully retain the full exact technical report and any directly relevant companion parts.
Have a qualified human-factors reviewer map definitions and experimental boundaries to the Reiyah mathematical specification.
Empirically validate any retained construct under a preregistered protocol before making a scientific claim.
